brief: The WSJ reports interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in Nvidia's financing of AI deals, but Huang had already begun closing the checkbook before his ouster: an August pause on revenue-share credit support, then a Berlin ultimatum telling neocloud CEOs to secure upfront customer payments or lose GPU allocations, since he could divert capacity to Musk instead. The stated driver: Nvidia's off-balance-sheet commitments hit $530bn (supply and capacity purchases $279bn, more than doubling in three months) just as hyperscalers drift toward rival chips, so funding buyers while still owing suppliers became unsustainable. Kress, who already cut Nvidia's OpenAI backstop in half, must now choose protecting the balance sheet over market share, since AMD, Google and Broadcom offer rivals similar financing terms. UBS's Arcuri estimates a pause could pull $50bn from the AI ecosystem; AI-issuer credit spreads have widened to roughly 140bps. Nebius's prepayment-funded capex model is framed as the template cash-burning neoclouds cannot copy. Venture-stage dependents such as Reflection AI and Thinking Machines face capital risk if Nvidia's equity checkbook also closes. Goldman still sees the selloff as a buying opportunity given cheap relative multiples, but names financing cost, not construction capacity, as the real constraint.
